purpose: Small robot-arm simulation exercise comparing camera observations; no execution yet.

source.reference: Dynamic Camera-Relation VLA Proposal, shared by a senior student
source.note: External learning reference; no ownership claim. The original proposal is not included in this repository. Magnitudes are reference-based draft choices; axes and signs still need verification.

geometry_convention.transform: T_A_B maps coordinates in frame B into frame A using column vectors.
geometry_convention.units: Translation in metres; angles in degrees in this configuration only.
geometry_convention.axes: Right-handed baseline wrist optical frame: +x right, +y down, +z forward. Convert explicitly from the simulator camera convention.
geometry_convention.composition: T_E_Cw_perturbed = T_E_Cw_baseline @ Delta; perturbation is expressed in the baseline camera frame.
geometry_convention.rotation_sign: Positive angle follows the right-hand rule about the stated axis.
geometry_convention.delta_definition: Delta = [R, t; 0, 1]. R rotates vectors first, then t translates them, both expressed in the baseline camera frame.
geometry_convention.dynamic_pose: T_B_Cw(t) = T_B_E(t) @ T_E_Cw_perturbed; camera remains rigidly attached during each episode.

completion_gate: Verify one simulator, robot and scene on the actual target machine.
Resolve camera parameters and check coordinate conversions.
Reuse initial scene states and record actual configuration.
Save real images, observations, visibility changes and errors.
